business_problem: Regis Aged Care needed to compress a daily clinical handover review that could take two to three hours for 200-plus pages of notes, without missing a single resident-level clinical signal.
solution_summary: Cognizant and Regis Aged Care built a generative AI assistant to compress daily handover review without losing key resident detail. The solution ingests more than 200 pages of clinical progress notes, processes them in segments, and reassembles the results through a custom prompt that produces structured summaries for each resident and answers ad hoc questions in a familiar chat interface. The proof of concept ran in two homes on Microsoft Copilot Studio with the authentication and security controls required for healthcare, then moved into full production across the Regis network after benchmarking against a registered-nurse baseline. Cognizant and Regis continue to tune the assistant against categories such as agitation, medication and infection, while change-management work helps clinicians adopt the tool as support rather than replacement. The design combines note ingestion, prompt orchestration, benchmarking and human trust-building so review time falls without compromising safety.

data_flow: Clinical progress notes are ingested, segmented for model processing, and then reassembled through a custom prompt that creates resident summaries and answers questions in a chat interface. Clinician-defined benchmarking compares the output with control answers and registered-nurse results, while production staff use the assistant in routine handovers across the Regis network.

business_outcome: Regis reduced handover review time from hours to under an hour, expanded the assistant from a two-home proof of concept into production across its network, and redirected clinician time toward resident care while maintaining strict safety standards.
